title: Steve Lewis and the piano contest won by his friend
summary: Asked about Steve Lewis, he recalls the boat contest won by his non-reading friend, and hearing Udell in honky-tonks.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And you stayed with George. Yeah I stayed with George. In California. I was going to ask you in particular about some more of the piano players, a lot of the guys I wouldn't know like you didn't because I wasn't there. But Steve Lewis, I know one time some friend of mine talked to you about Steve Lewis. Can you tell us something about him?

Well I was pretty young and I didn't know too much about Steve outside he was a good piano player. And he could sing all kind of risky numbers and different things like that. And he played with P-Rone's band. But I didn't know too much about Steve. I saw him a couple of times. Because they had a contest on the Estora for the best piano player and my little friend that taught me, started me off playing, Bourbon, won the contest from Steve Lewis and Walter Pichon, who were the top piano players in New Orleans at the time. I know. But this guy was so fast he was a great piano man.

He couldn't read a note as big as a boxcar. No. But man, he played anything he'd hear. Anything. Don't care what it was. He played. And that's where I saw Steve. I had the, when I was little we had, I used to live around where they had these what you would call hunky-tongs. And they had the one on Orleans near Liberty that they called the Blues Breakers. And I had the pleasure of listening to a fellow by the name of Udell playing. Who used to make, I don't know, I just know about Udell. He made piano rolls. The best talks about it.
